hints: Look closely at cell shape and position. Label 4 shows tall, tightly packed columns near the top of the leaf, while label 3 shows rounded, loosely spaced cells near the bottom.
Remember the leaf rule for position: xylem is on the upper (adaxial) side of the vein and phloem is on the lower (abaxial) side, and palisade is always upper for light capture.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two mesophyll layers**

Great start, look at the shape of the photosynthetic cells. Label 4 points to long, columnar, tightly packed cells just under the upper epidermis. That is classic palisade mesophyll for absorbing light.

Label 3 points to small, rounded cells with big air spaces near the lower epidermis. That is classic spongy mesophyll for gas exchange.

**Sort out xylem and phloem in the vein**

Now focus on the vascular bundle in the middle. Label 1 is the upper group of larger, open, thick-walled vessels. Label 2 is the lower group of smaller, densely stained cells.

In a dicot leaf vein, xylem is adaxial (toward the upper surface) and phloem is abaxial (toward the lower surface). So 1 = xylem, 2 = phloem.

**Match to the table**

Putting it together: 1 is xylem, 2 is phloem, 3 is spongy mesophyll, 4 is palisade mesophyll.

That combination is option D only.

options.A: Incorrect because 1 and 2 are reversed and 3 and 4 are reversed. 1 is upper xylem not phloem, and 4 is upper palisade not spongy.
options.B: Incorrect because 1 and 2 are reversed. 1 is xylem on the upper side and 2 is phloem on the lower side, not the other way round.
options.C: Incorrect because 3 and 4 are reversed. 4 is the columnar palisade layer and 3 is the loose spongy layer, not the other way round.
options.D: Correct. 1 is xylem (upper), 2 is phloem (lower), 3 is spongy mesophyll (lower, loose), 4 is palisade mesophyll (upper, columnar).
